explanations.answer: Very much of the land remains to be possessed
explanations.explanation: That's exactly what the LORD says. "You are old and well along in years, but very much of the land remains to be possessed." (Joshua 13:1) Joshua, Israel's leader, has done a LOT, and there's still a lot left. I know that feeling, friend. You finish one tray and the counter is still covered.

explanations.answer: All of the land has now been possessed
explanations.explanation: I get why you'd think that, with Joshua winning so much. But the LORD says the opposite: "…very much of the land remains to be possessed." (Joshua 13:1) Nobody gets to hang up the apron yet. The work isn't done, even when the leader is old.

explanations.answer: The land must wait for a new leader
explanations.explanation: Joshua is old, so that's a fair guess. But the LORD doesn't mention a new leader here. He talks to Joshua about the land and says, "…very much of the land remains to be possessed." (Joshua 13:1) The job is still sitting on Joshua's counter.

Yes, baker! The LORD says, "I Myself will drive out before the Israelites." (Joshua 13:6) That covers the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians. He doesn't ask Israel to do it alone. He says He will do it.

Joshua's army has done plenty of fighting, so I see the guess. But look at who the LORD names here: "I Myself will drive out before the Israelites." (Joshua 13:6) He puts Himself right in that sentence. Joshua's job in the verse is to divide the land by lot.

explanations.answer: The tribes east of the Jordan
explanations.explanation: Those tribes already have their land from Moses, so they're a tempting pick. But the LORD doesn't hand this job to them. He says, "I Myself will drive out before the Israelites." (Joshua 13:6) The answer is right there in the first words of that promise.

True! The LORD says, "Be sure to divide it by lot as an inheritance to Israel, as I have commanded you." (Joshua 13:6) Even with land still to be taken, He wants it divided. That tells me He's serious about what He promised.

This one is true, friend. The LORD says, "Be sure to divide it by lot as an inheritance to Israel, as I have commanded you." (Joshua 13:6) The land isn't all taken yet, and He still tells Joshua to divide it. I like that you were careful, though.

explanations.answer: Nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh
explanations.explanation: That's it! The LORD says, "Now therefore divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh." (Joshua 13:7) Nine plus a half. The math is a little strange, but the Bible says it, so I'm not arguing.

Twelve tribes is the number everybody remembers. But the LORD says this land goes "to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh." (Joshua 13:7) The rest had already received their land from Moses, east of the Jordan (Joshua 13:8).

explanations.answer: The tribes of Reuben and Gad
explanations.explanation: Close, but that's the wrong direction. Reuben and Gad had already received their inheritance from Moses beyond the Jordan (Joshua 13:8). This new land is for "the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh." (Joshua 13:7) Reuben and Gad were already sitting on their porch.

I see why you'd say that, since the east was Moses' conquest. But the text says, "…the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites." (Joshua 13:13) So the answer is false. And it adds that Geshur and Maacath "dwell among the Israelites to this day."

False is right, baker! "…the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites. So Geshur and Maacath dwell among the Israelites to this day." (Joshua 13:13) They stayed put and became neighbors. Awkward, but that's what the verse says.

explanations.answer: The food offerings to the LORD
explanations.explanation: Yes! "The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:14) Levi gets no land, but they get what's given to the LORD. Their share comes straight from the LORD's own table.

Gold sounds like a nice inheritance, but the text never mentions it for Levi. It says, "The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:14) Their share was never about treasure.

Sihon's cities are real, but they went to Reuben and Gad (Joshua 13:21, 27). Levi gets something different: "The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:14) Sihon, king of the Amorites, is not on Levi's list.
